data.title: 2026-27 Missouri Valley Conference preview | The IX Basketball
data.content:
“I think with the players that we’re returning — Trista Fayta, who had a record-setting year for a point guard, she’s top 10 in the country in assists, and Nevaeh Thomas, who got injured really early in our season, she is one of the best post players in our league. I think she’s one of the best post players in mid-major basketball,” Gillespie told The IX Sports. “And then we bring back two starting guards in sophomores Jaeden Pratt and Grace Nelson.” [...] “So, from a point guard perspective, we were taking applications and plugging people in,” she added. “Credit to those players for being able to do what they were asked to do, but it’s not what people were used to as far as Drake women’s basketball and the success and lineage and history that we’ve had. But we’re just really excited about taking the next steps forward.”

The upside of dealing with injuries is the experience gained for players up and down the roster. [...] Drake already faced an uphill battle last season after losing four key players to graduation, including two-time MVC Player of the Year Katie Dinnebier. But then the injury bug hit and the Bulldogs could never recover, posting its first losing season since 2012-13.
